category: Zero-dependency in-memory cache for TypeScript/JavaScript — TTL expiration, LRU eviction, wildcard pattern deletion, and a @cached method-memoization decorator

competitors.note: The default 'simple in-memory cache with TTL' people reach for; huge downloads, no decorator, no wildcard delete
The canonical LRU implementation; extremely popular, LRU-focused, lower-level API
Multi-backend key-value store (memory + Redis/SQLite/etc.); broader scope, but overlaps on 'simple cache' searches

non_goals: A distributed / multi-process cache (Redis-style) — this is in-process memory only
Persistence across restarts — it's ephemeral by design
A pluggable multi-backend store layer (that's keyv's niche)

repo_triage._comment: Public repo — GITHUB_TOKEN raises rate limits; public-read fallback works without it. Surfaces open PRs/issues NOT opened by github_handle, and threads awaiting your reply since the previous last_run.

self_features: Zero runtime dependencies; works in Node and the browser, TypeScript-first
LRU eviction with a max-size bound
Wildcard pattern deletion (invalidate many keys at once)
Aimed at API-response caching, session storage, and hot-path memoization
